statement: Fix a preceding finite sequence as in Theorem 2.12. Suppose a temporary Hamiltonian is diagonal in a common collection of site axes, with coefficients given by an exclusion calculation. Require its local Hamiltonian matrices and every aggregate-input derivative to have polynomial bounds as in Definition 2.11. In a cut branch let HD(a) denote the sum of the Hamiltonian terms affected by scalar boundary input a, truncated beyond its finite influence distance and conjugated by the preceding subtree circuit. Assume explicitly that HD(−a) = PHD(a)P, PΩ = Ω, (2.30) where P is the joint spin/seed symmetry. The first two boundary derivatives have smooth limits Hα = limD ∂αHD(0) and Hαλ = limD ∂α∂λHD(0), and Hα is centered. These limits concern the 22 response derivatives; no limit for the extensive HD(0) is required. The change in its D child branches when zero boundary input is replaced by a/ √ D is D X j=1  HD(a/ √ D) − HD(0) (j) . Its smooth limit is X α aαq(HαΩ) + 1 2 X α,λ aαaλ⟨Hαλ⟩0. (2.31) The correction is realized as the self-adjoint generator of the limiting time group of the child cut ratios; the display specifies its action on the smooth domain. We use the same realization after commuting substitution and for the correction generators below. The same formula applies recursively to lower cut responses and to their input jets. It is continuous with the smooth bounds of Theorem 2.12, for a fixed finite list of channels. Commuting parameter operators may replace a under the same exclusions. In particular, if a sequence of such correction generators Rj satisfies ∥Rjξ∥ ≤ δj∥Wrξ∥ with δj → 0, then ∥(eitRj − 1)ξ∥ ≤ |t|δj∥Wr ξ∥. (2.32) If their exponentials and adjoints also have uniform smooth bounds, these errors tend to zero in every fixed lower graph norm and may be inserted in a fixed surrounding sequence.
